subtopics.title: The Field Concept and the Rules of Field Lines

questions.question: An electric field is defined as:
options: A region of space in which an electric charge experiences a force
The path electrons take through a wire
The force between two touching charges
A region where only positive charges may exist

questions.question: The direction of the field at a point is defined by the force on:
options: A small positive test charge placed there

questions.question: Field lines never cross because:
options: Crossing lines would repel each other
Lines are drawn too far apart to meet
A single point cannot have two directions of force
Crossing is only allowed for magnetic fields

questions.question: In a field-line diagram, closely bunched lines indicate:
options: A region where the field is zero
A region where the field is strong

subtopics.title: Field Strength from Force — E Equals F Over q

questions.question: Electric field strength is defined as:
options: The force per unit positive charge at a point, E = F/q, in N·C⁻¹
The total force a source charge can produce
The charge per unit force, q/F
The energy stored in the field

questions.question: A +4 × 10⁻⁶ C charge at P feels 0,02 N north. The field at P is:
That same 5 000 N·C⁻¹ field acts on an electron. The force on it is:
options: Zero, since electrons are too small

questions.question: Doubling the test charge placed at a point changes the field strength there to:
options: Unchanged — the field belongs to the location, not the visitor

subtopics.title: Field of a Point Charge — E Equals k Q Over r Squared

questions.question: In deriving E = kQ/r² from Coulomb's law, the test charge q:
options: Cancels out, leaving the field dependent only on the source and distance
Appears squared in the final formula

questions.question: The field 0,2 m from a +8 μC point charge is:
options: 1,8 × 10⁶ N·C⁻¹, directed away from the charge

questions.question: Tripling the distance from a point source changes the field to:
E = F/q versus E = kQ/r²: the correct division of labour is:
options: F/q for positive charges, kQ/r² for negative ones
They are interchangeable in every question
kQ/r² only works in a vacuum
F/q when a force on a visiting charge is known; kQ/r² when a source charge and distance are known

subtopics.title: Fields from More Than One Charge

questions.question: The net field at a point near several charges is found by:
options: Vector-adding the field each source creates there, each computed at its own distance
Adding all the source charges first, then using kQ/r² once

questions.question: P lies midway between A (+4 μC) and B (−6 μC), 0,3 m from each. A's contribution at P is:
The net field at P is:
options: 1 × 10⁶ N·C⁻¹ directed from A toward B
1 × 10⁶ N·C⁻¹ directed from B toward A

questions.question: Between two LIKE charges, the point of zero net field lies:
options: Outside the pair, beyond the larger charge
Nowhere — like charges have no zero point
Between them, closer to the weaker charge

subtopics.title: The Invisible Cushion Around Every Charge

questions.question: In the cushion picture, a second charge entering the region responds to:
options: The cushion (field) at the exact spot where it stands
The faraway first charge directly, by touch
The average of the whole cushion

questions.question: The probe used to map a field is:
A lone positive charge's field map looks like:
options: Spikes radiating outward, like a spiky seed pod

subtopics.title: How Hard Is the Shove at This Spot?

questions.question: Quoting the raw force at a spot is unhelpful because:
options: The force depends on the probe's charge, so it describes the probe, not the place
Forces cannot be measured in fields
The force is always the same everywhere
Newtons are not defined inside fields

questions.question: The rand-per-litre analogy says field strength is like:
options: A unit price — newtons for every coulomb, independent of the amount bought

questions.question: A spot rated 5 000 N·C⁻¹ delivers to a 4 × 10⁻⁶ C visitor a force of:
A negative visitor in a mapped field is shoved:
options: Along the arrows, like a positive charge

subtopics.title: When Two Charges Both Have a Say

questions.question: Between a positive charge (left) and a negative charge (right), the two field votes at a point between them:
options: Both point right — they add, making the field strong
Point in opposite directions — they cancel

questions.question: Between two EQUAL positive charges, the net field is zero:
If the two like charges are UNEQUAL, the dead spot shifts:
options: Toward the weaker charge, where its fading voice can match the stronger one's

questions.question: The correct bookkeeping for a two-charge field point is:
options: Add the charges, then compute one field
Compute one field using the average distance
Use only the nearer charge's field
Compute each contribution at its own distance, draw the two arrows, then add or subtract as they agree or clash
